newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus ministers resign, reshuffle announced.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus ministers resign, reshuffle announced.

text.p: The Cyprus cabinet resigned on Tuesday to make way for a government reshuffle 10 months before the latest date that presidential elections are due on the eastern mediterranean island.
The new composition of the centre-right government will be announced later on Tuesday or early on Wednesday, government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides told reporters.

"The President of the Republic announced to members of the Council of Ministers (cabinet) that he has decided to exercise his constitutional right to proceed with a reshuffle of the government," said Cassoulides after a brief cabinet session.
The local media has reported that Cassoulides is likely to be appointed foreign minister to replace Alecos Michaelides.
"If he (the president) has reached the decision to proceed with a reshuffle it is a political act for government renewal and not because he has any grievances with any minister," Cassoulides added.
It is the first cabinet reshuffle since Clerides, a veteran right-wing politician and founder of the Democratic Rally party, was elected president of the island for a five year term in February 1993.
Media reports have speculated that five of the eleven ministers, appointees of the Democratic Party which is a junior partner in the government, will be unaffected by the reshuffle.
